items.name: Quantum DC pauses 1,200 MW Tungkillo AI data centre near Adelaide; will not file development application this year - third Australian project halted in weeks
items.headline: Quantum DC pauses 1,200 MW Tungkillo AI data centre near Adelaide; will not file development application this year - third Australian project halted in weeks
items.source: ABC News (Isabella Carbone), 2026-11-12 08:14 AEDT; Bloomberg via Energy Connects, 2026-11-12; read via WebFetch
items.claim: Quantum DC (CEO Alby Tomassi) paused its proposed 1,200 MW AI data centre plus associated energy infrastructure at Tungkillo, ~41 km east of Adelaide, and will not seek development approval this year, saying 'we misread the strength of feeling about this proposal' after 350+ residents contacted the company with 432 consolidated questions on water, energy, farmland and bushfire. Bloomberg (via Energy Connects, 11-12) calls it at least the third Australian data-centre development delayed in recent weeks, after NEXTDC's Melbourne project and Stockland's abandoned Sydney plans. Project cost not disclosed; company has not ruled out proceeding later after an independent expert panel reviews the studies.

items.name: Bernstein: of 586 GW planned North American data-center capacity only ~199 GW (34%) will be built; 387 GW removed for stage/tenant-credit/developer/state risk; Texas 2027 unstarted 11 GW -> 0.3 GW expected
items.headline: Bernstein: of 586 GW planned North American data-center capacity only ~199 GW (34%) will be built; 387 GW removed for stage/tenant-credit/developer/state risk; Texas 2027 unstarted 11 GW -> 0.3 GW expected
items.source: BigGo Finance summarising Bernstein research note, 2026-11-12 10:55 UTC; read via WebFetch (analyst estimate, not a company deferral)
items.claim: Bernstein estimates that of 586 GW of planned North American data-center capacity only about 199 GW (~34%) will actually be built; the ~387 GW haircut breaks down into development stage (198 GW), tenant credit (113 GW), developer strength (48 GW) and state political risk (28 GW). Only 87 GW has broken ground (86% of that expected to complete); of the ~497 GW still at announcement stage only about a quarter is expected to materialise. In Texas, of 18 GW scheduled for 2028 but not under construction Bernstein expects 5 GW, and of 11 GW scheduled for 2027 but not started only 0.3 GW. Bernstein frames this as projects that were never feasible rather than cancellations; the 11-12 daily digest adds that neoclouds are only 4% of the credible pipeline.

items.name: Bloomberg: OpenAI cut target valuation to $1.25T from $1.4T and trimmed funding goal by a third after investor pushback; VCs applying lower revenue multiples over past two weeks, advising startups to take lower valuations
items.headline: Bloomberg: OpenAI cut target valuation to $1.25T from $1.4T and trimmed funding goal by a third after investor pushback; VCs applying lower revenue multiples over past two weeks, advising startups to take lower valuations
items.source: Bloomberg (Rebecca Torrence, Natasha Mascarenhas), 2026-11-11, updated 15:42; read via Spokesman-Review syndication by WebFetch (Bloomberg original robots_disallowed)
items.claim: Bloomberg reports that OpenAI, which in late September sought at least $30bn at a $1.4T valuation (prior mark $852bn), lowered its target to $1.25T and cut its funding goal by about a third after some investors found the terms too lofty and market conditions weakened (sources; OpenAI declined comment). Tomasz Tunguz (Theory Ventures) says investors have applied more conservative revenue multiples in AI funding talks over the past two weeks; Howard Morgan (B Capital) says he is telling many startups 'that's too high given your current revenues'. Anthropic's IPO is pitched at a lower-than-expected $1.4T fully diluted (bankers weighing $1.5T+; some had expected ~$2T); Jai Das (Sapphire) warns a bad debut means 'some companies are going to go out of business'. No closed down-round is named; the underlying $11bn-at-$1.25T report dates to 11-06.

items.headline: FT (via Newsquawk): widening divide in eurozone sovereign bond markets between highly indebted France/Belgium and safer borrowers like Germany - no spread levels given
items.source: Newsquawk headline relaying FT, 2026-11-11 05:05 UTC (= 2026-11-10 22:05 MST, before gate cutoff); read via WebFetch
items.claim: Newsquawk relays an FT report that a widening divide has opened in eurozone sovereign bond markets, separating highly indebted countries such as France and Belgium from safer borrowers such as Germany; Newsquawk's own note attributes it to France's deficit/debt path and Belgium's debt stock and says the ECB backstop limits tail outcomes. The page carries no OAT-Bund or Belgium-Bund spread levels or bp changes; the FT original was not fetched. Robeco (11-05, outside gate) separately said French spreads 'have risen again recently' on budget negotiations and election polls, with debt possibly reaching 137% of GDP by 2030.
